name: Control arm
summary: A hinged arm that connects the wheel to the car's frame. It lets the wheel move up and down while keeping it in place.
whatItDoes: It locates the wheel, stopping it from moving forward, backward or sideways, while still letting it travel up and down.
howItWorks: The inner end pivots on rubber bushings mounted to the subframe or body. The outer end carries a ball joint that connects to the steering knuckle, so the wheel can move up and down and also turn for steering.
failureSymptoms: Clunks over bumps or when braking
Visible cracks in the rubber bushings
safetyNotes: Many rubber bushings must be tightened with the suspension at normal ride height, or they can tear. Check your manual.
Have the wheel alignment checked afterwards.
